You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

## Summary of the Patch

This patch fixes a null pointer dereference crash in the VMware kernel mode setting (KMS) driver that occurred on hardware version 10 when using 3D (surface-backed) framebuffers. The root cause is that hardware version 10 does not support GB Surfaces, so there is no backing buffer (`bo`) for such framebuffers, but the code unconditionally tried to reserve and operate on the `bo`.

### Modifications in each file:

**`drivers/gpu/drm/vmwgfx/vmwgfx_kms.c`**  
- In the `vmw_kms_fb_create` function, the calls to `ttm_bo_reserve()`, `vmw_bo_dirty_add()`, and the subsequent dirty-allocation logic (including `ttm_bo_unreserve()`) were wrapped inside an `if (bo)` guard.  
- Previously, these operations were always executed regardless of whether `bo` was NULL. Now they are only performed when `bo` is non-NULL.

### Relationship of changes:

The sole change is the addition of a NULL-pointer check for the `bo` variable. This prevents a dereference of a NULL pointer that would occur on hardware version 10 when a surface-backed framebuffer is created without a backing buffer. The rest of the function flow (error handling, return value) remains unaffected because when `bo` is NULL, the guarded operations are simply skipped.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>ttm_bo_reserve(&bo->tbo, false, false, NULL);</text>
<text>ret = vmw_bo_dirty_add(bo);</text>
<text>ttm_bo_unreserve(&bo->tbo);</text>
Reason:
On hardware version 10, there are no GB Surfaces, so surface-backed framebuffers have no backing buffer (`bo` is NULL). The original code unconditionally called `ttm_bo_reserve()` and subsequent operations on `bo` without a NULL check, causing a null pointer dereference and driver crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>if (bo) {</text>
<text>	ttm_bo_reserve(&bo->tbo, false, false, NULL);</text>
<text>	ret = vmw_bo_dirty_add(bo);</text>
<text>	if (!ret && surface && surface->res.func->dirty_alloc) {</text>
<text>		surface->res.coherent = true;</text>
<text>		ret = surface->res.func->dirty_alloc(&surface->res);</text>
<text>	}</text>
<text>	ttm_bo_unreserve(&bo->tbo);</text>
<text>}</text>
Reason:
The fix adds a NULL check for `bo` before performing any operations on it, preventing the null pointer dereference that caused the crash. This ensures that the code only reserves the buffer and modifies dirty state when `bo` is valid.
